brief: Evidence for the user decision: raise the 35B CUDA recipe prefill_chunk from 2048 to 8192 now that fp8-lt is default (#125)? CPU references (-g4k, longer/other splits), gates at 8192 (KL goldens, reuse, acc-short, acc-4k, batch_cuda_real + long), prefill vs vLLM at 1k/4k/16k x3 interleaved, 4-stream aggregate decode and ITL at both chunks. Default not changed.
hypothesis: Chunk 8192 keeps every accuracy gate (thresholds unchanged) and gives +6-11% prefill at 4k/16k; the price is a longer decode stall when a prompt prefills beside decoding streams, because the busy chunk follows the solo chunk.

summary: Chunk 8192 on the 35B CUDA recipe gives +6.4 % (4k) and +11.1 % (16k) solo prefill (+8.9 % / +5.8 % vs vLLM, against +2.2 % / -4.8 % at 2048) and passes every numeric accuracy gate with thresholds unchanged. Two things stop the one-line recipe edit: qualify acc-4k fails structurally (no 4k-golden prompt can cross an 8192 chunk), and the busy chunk follows the solo chunk, so the worst decode pause under batching grows 336 -> 590 ms (4k) and 383 -> 1264 ms (16k); --busy-chunk 2048 removes that. New f64 CPU continue oracles (long_code_4k -g4k, 12k s12062/s9500/s6000) are committed; the s6000 one fails a hand-run chunk-2048 reuse on a near-tie prompt (not an 8192 result). Recipe default not changed; decision left to the user.
lessons: The reuse gate finds oracles in the golden's own directory: a lane that adds oracles to a shared golden dir changes what other lanes' reuse runs report. Use a lane-private golden dir on the Sparks.

qualify's acc-4k runs reuse inside accuracy --mode all at the plan chunk; a recipe chunk above the longest 4k-golden prompt (4631) fails it with 'nothing ran'. The separate capped run (min(chunk,1024)) is fine.
The busy chunk follows the solo chunk on CUDA: a recipe chunk change is also a batching latency change. localeval --concurrency has no ITL; scripts/c8k/itl4.py keeps every inter-token interval.

Oracle-relative reuse on a near-tie prompt: whichever of cold/warm lands on the far side of an unstable position is far from the oracle; the rule fails when it is the warm one. cold 2048 vs cold 1024 differ by KL 4.2e-2 on the same rows.
Editing a shell script while fleetq has it running breaks the running copy (bash reads incrementally): the speed window aborted after retro was already down.
macOS has no timeout(1); the endor-side scripts must not use it.
